styles.era: 10-character serials, letter + digit + letter + 7 digits, year only
styles.notes: Page: year = '2nd-4th numerical digits combined', month = 3rd character letter (chart below). SPLIT-YEAR READING (coordinator review): a contiguous 2nd-4th character read would include the month letter (0K5, not digits), and digit-only counting would give a 3-digit '589', invalid as a year — so the only coherent reading of the page's own text is the two numerical digits flanking the month letter, 2nd character '0' and 4th character '5', combined as '05' -> 2005 (split positions [[1,2],[3,4]], default 1960 floor: 1905 below floor, 2005 only candidate). Month letter mapping appears nowhere in page text (page images are serial-number/data-plate photos, no letter table), so month is null and the style ships year-only pending the image pass.
Page: year = 1st-2nd digits ([0,2] = '97' -> 1997), month = 3rd-4th digits ([2,4] = '10' = October). All digits, so character and digit-only counting coincide.

styles.era: 9- or 10-digit all-numeric serials, used prior to 1992, month + year
styles.notes: Page LIST gives the example as 9 digits (018812345) while the DETAIL heading gives it as 10 digits (0188123456, 'Used prior to 1992') with a 10-character description; month = 1st-2nd digits, year = 3rd-4th digits. LIST-VS-DETAIL DUAL FORM: both forms decode identically under the stated positions (month '01' = January, year '88' -> 1988) and the combined pattern ^\d{9,10}$ is disjoint from all other styles in this file, so both forms ship with both page examples.
